(i) we provide the first coset for \kMeans with missing values, and (ii) we show that this coreset is a \emph{universal} coreset, meaning that it approximates any clustering objective that can be written as a convex function of the distances between points and centers

(a) we show that the problem of coreset construction for clustering with missing values is hard; (b) we design a new algorithm to compute coresets for \kMeans and \kMedoids that is based on a novel notion of a "partial" coreset that only needs to $(1+\epsilon)^2$-approximate the objective for every set of $k$ centers and that (c) we show how to combine partial coresets with a novel "partial" sampling technique

(1) we provide the first coresets for clustering points that have multiple missing coordinates; (2) our coreset is a $(1+\epsilon,1+\epsilon)$ approximation for any number of missing coordinates; (3) our coreset has size $n^{1+o(1)}$ and can be computed in near-linear time.
